title: AI Ethics
intro: These stories connect Texas data-center growth and AI accountability with community access, human connection, energy use, and local oversight.

items.title: What Texas Turning Blue Could Mean for Data Centers and the AI Industry in the U.S.
items.description: IBTimes reports that Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on pausing new data-center approvals until stronger protections are enacted, raising questions about how Texas balances AI infrastructure growth with public oversight.

items.title: Gina Hinojosa on data centers and immigration
items.description: A New York Times video interview with Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, published alongside coverage of data-center policy and immigration.

links.label: Watch the New York Times video

items.title: Pflugerville adopts new policy for AI, surveillance technology and data privacy
items.description: After ending its Flock Safety contract following questions about camera-data searches, Pflugerville adopted a SAFE Technology policy covering AI, surveillance and data sharing. It includes risk tiers, City Council review of high-risk tools, resident oversight, limits on data use and annual public reporting. Because AI and surveillance tools can affect privacy and residents’ rights, Round Rock should adopt enforceable guardrails and public reporting like Pflugerville instead of leaving procurement to an unchecked free-market approach.

items.title: Remember the 'dumb carpooling idea'? It's happening now in Austin.
items.description: An Austin-area program is offering incentives for I-35 commuters to carpool, a current local example of shared rides being used to address congestion.

items.title: The problem with IRL: Is any of it real?
items.description: Mashable reports that the separate IRL social app shut down in 2023 after an investigation found that 95% of its claimed 20 million users were automated or bots. Three years later, AI-generated slop and apps with outlandish claims make the trust question more urgent. IRL.group is real and distinct from that app. Is the AI boom repeating the dot-com bust, when some startups rushed to sell everything online—even toilet paper—before proving lasting value?

items.title: IRL.group: a home for local creators
items.description: IRL.group is launching commercial and nonprofit pilots to help fine-tune the project. These pilots look different from the increasingly crowded events-on-a-map newsletter concept.
